title: The use and domestication of Theobroma cacao during the mid-Holocene in the upper Amazon
version: Nature Ecology & Evolution 2 (2018), pp. 1879–1888, DOI 10.1038/s41559-018-0697-x. Version-of-record article and supplement, mirrored PDF.

passages.locator: p. 1881, Table 1 note a and PLD-005; Fig. 2d
passages.note: The charred residue from PLD-005, Beta-312078, was directly AMS dated to 5440–5310 cal BP in Table 1. The table reports theobromine, diagnostic Theobroma starch and a T. cacao-specific signal from DNA capture.

passages.locator: pp. 1880–1882, Fig. 2a–b, Table 1 and discussion of DNA capture
passages.note: PLD-001 and PLD-002 are stirrup-spout bottles from separate later tomb contexts. Both Table 1 and prose place them around 4000 cal BP, with different interval estimates.

lineage: Original analysis of a single site assemblage. Analytical methods are independently informative. The direct AMS target was the charred residue on the early sherd.
